svg.text: Tokens: from characters to IDs to answers
Example used throughout: "What is the capital of Bangladesh?" → "Dhaka."
Part A · How text splitting evolved
Network must learn spelling → words → meaning
Expects too much from the network
The trade-off: smaller pieces = smaller vocabulary but longer sequences · bigger pieces = shorter sequences but huge vocabulary. Subwords balance both.
Part B · The full token pipeline, step by step
Left: the flow · Middle: what happens · Right: our example
Steps 1–5 run before the model: no AI, just rules + a lookup table

text.tspan: Input text
You type a question. To a computer this is just a string of
characters, stored as UTF-8 bytes (numbers 0–255). A neural
network can't use text directly; it needs IDs from a fixed list.

svg.text: W=57 h=68 a=61 t=74 space=20 (hex) · 34 characters

text.tspan: Pre-split into chunks
A simple rule (regex) first cuts the text at spaces and
punctuation, so merges never cross word boundaries. The space is
kept on the FRONT of the next word (␣).

svg.text: 7 chunks · BPE now works inside each chunk

text.tspan: BPE merging
Each chunk starts as single bytes. The tokenizer applies its
learned merge rules (most frequent pairs from training data, in
ranked order) again and again until no rule fits.
Tokens
The final pieces are the tokens. Common words = 1 token. Less
common words = a few known pieces. Same text → always the same
tokens.
Vocabulary lookup →
Token IDs
Each token is looked up in the vocabulary (a dictionary of
~50k–200k entries) and replaced by its integer ID. This list is
what the model receives, and what the API counts and bills.
Embedding
Inside the model, each ID selects one row of the embedding table
→ a vector of thousands of numbers representing meaning.
Position info is added so word order is known.
Transformer layers
Attention lets every token look at the others ("capital" +
"Bangla" + "desh"). After N layers the model scores EVERY
vocabulary entry; softmax turns scores into probabilities.
Pick the next token
One token is chosen from the probabilities (sampling).
Temperature controls randomness: low = almost always the top
choice, high = more creative.
Detokenize → text
The chosen ID is turned back into text with the same vocabulary
(reverse lookup) and streamed to you immediately.

svg.text: shown to you right away → that's why answers "stream"

text.tspan: Repeat or stop
The new ID is appended to the context and the model runs again
from step 6. It stops when it picks the special <end> token or
hits max_tokens.

svg.text: text → chunks → BPE merges → tokens → IDs → vectors → transformer → probabilities → pick ID → text → repeat until <end>
Rule of thumb: 1 token ≈ 4 English characters ≈ ¾ word · Bangla/Arabic often use 2–4× more tokens · You pay for input + output tokens
Token splits, IDs and probabilities are illustrative. Every model family has its own tokenizer and vocabulary.
